chunks: "Whoever forgets one prayer from among the prayers of his day, and does not know which prayer it is, he should perform two rak'ahs, three, and four."

And this hadith was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from 'Ali ibn Asbat, from more than one of our companions, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام:

key_terms.صَلَاةً: a salat (prayer), referring here to one of the daily obligatory prayers
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: the same wording or meaning as the previous report
key_terms.يَوْمِهِ: his day, meaning the set of daily prayers

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they forgot one daily salat (prayer) but do not know which prayer it was?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who has forgotten a single daily salat (prayer) but does not know which one it was. The instruction is to perform prayers of two, three, and four rak'ahs to cover the possible missed obligation, reflecting precision in fulfilling uncertain devotional duties.
